Commentary.Commentary: We are set for the chase to begin! The Irish fielders walk out to the middle. Aiden Markram and Janneman Malan will open the batting. Craig Young will start with the ball. Here we go...

Right then! 291 runs in 300 balls is what South Africa need to win the game. Remember, they don't have Quinton de Kock so the other batters will have to take the responsibility of getting quick runs at the top. To be honest, they have a very good batting line up and would fancy their chances given the nice batting conditions. For the Irish, early wickets remain the key if they want to make South Africa sweat. Do join us for a while as the chase comes our way!

Keshav Maharaj is down for a chat, Maharaj says that his first spell was good but he could have been a bit proactive. Adds that the pitch is really good so the batters should be able to chase it down. Further adds that this is a par score and they need to keep wickets in hand while chasing. Also mentions that Andy Balbirnie batted really well to set the platform for Tector and Dockrell.

South Africa did not have the best of days with the ball. Their pacers started well and even created opportunities at the start but their fielders could not hold on. The spin duo of Maharaj and Shamsi bowled well in the middle overs, they took a wicket each and also dried up the boundaries. But in the death overs, their pacers were taken apart by some brilliant hitting by the Irish. The two spinners gave 92 in their 20 overs and took two wickets. While their pacers went for 195 in their 30 overs and took 3 wickets, 2 of which came in the last over. Overall, it was a disappointing day with the ball for them.

Ireland had a good start with the bat. Stirling and Balbirnie provided them with a 50-run stand with the latter getting boundaries more frequently. They did lose the momentum in the middle overs as Stirling and McBrine both fell to spinners and they weren't able to rotate the strike as freely as before. But Balbirnie held one end together and batted really well to get to his ton. Tector started off slowly at the start but teed off towards the end. He along with Dockrell provided them with a very good finish. Tector got 79 and Dockrell got 45 to get them to 290.

What a fantastic batting performance that was by Ireland. They have put on a very good score and would hope that their bowlers defend it. Temba Bavuma mentioned at the toss that this ground would be tough to defend on but his batters will have to bat quite well if they want to win this.

Stirling was dropped two times as well but Maharaj made sure he doesn't make most of it. The Irish captain is looking in good form as he is middling everything and keeping the scoreboard ticking. For the South Africans, they have to be stronger in the fielding department and start chipping wickets in regular intervals.

Yorker length, on leg pole. Stirling digs it out in time.
Length ball, on off. Defended out to cover.
Too full in length, on off. Paul Stirling pushes it to mid off.
A good length ball, angling down. Paul Stirling misses his flick.
Touch fuller, on middle. Kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Boundaries are flowing now with ease for the Irish batters! A length ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie clips it past short fine leg for a boundary.
A length ball, on middle. Defended out.
On middle, on a length, flicked away to square leg for a single.
Good length ball, around off. Blocked out.
FOUR! Up and over! Full and wide outside off. Stirling goes for it and hits it over the point fielder for a boundary.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! A length ball, outside off. Andy Balbirnie dabs it past point for four runs.
FOUR! Crunched! A length ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie punches off the back foot through covers for a boundary.

Review time! South Africa have reviewed this for caught behind. There is a gap between the bat and the ball, there is a spike as the ball passes the pads. They check for LBW, but the ball is going over the stumps.

NOT OUT! South Africa lose their review! A back of a length ball, angling on middle. Balbirnie looks to push from his crease. Gets something on it as the ball goes to the keeper, who takes the catch and immediately appeals for caught behind, but the umpire is unmoved. South Africa take the review. But the Ultra Edge shows it clipped the pads. Ball Tracker confirms wickets missing as they check for LBW.
FOUR! Welcome boundary! A short of a length ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie stands tall and pulls it away, not quite from the middle of the bat but enough for it to race away to the fence.
Shorter ball, outside off. Left alone.
Back of a length, around off. Blocked from the crease by Andy Balbirnie.
A length ball, outside off. Shoulders arms to it.

DROPPED AGAIN! Paul Stirling gets a second life and it's hard to believe that David Miller drops it! A length ball, outside off. Paul Stirling drives it uppishly towards cover. David Miller there leaps up, gets his hand on the ball but can't grab it. How costly will this SECOND life prove to be?
Again a fuller delivery, around off. Pushed to mid off.
Another full ball, on off. Andy Balbirnie pushes it wide of covers for a single.
Tad fuller, around off. Andy pushes it on the off side.
A length ball, outside off. Andy Balbirnie looks to push at it but misses.
Back of a length, on off. Angling back in and Stirling gets hit on the pads.
FOUR! Insult to injury for Anrich Nortje! But this is a lovely shot by Paul Stirling. Good length ball, on off. Stirling leans into it and punches it to the extra cover fence.
Length ball, way outside off. Left alone.

DROPPED AT SECOND SLIP! Aiden Markram just can't stick the ball to his hands!  A back of a length ball, on middle. Paul Stirling looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge towards the second slip where Aiden Markram dives across the first slip gets his hand on the ball but pops it out on the first attempt, attempts again but drops it again. Paul Stirling survives.
Again beaten! Beauty of a delivery from Anrich Nortje! A short of a length ball, outside off. Paul Stirling looks to defend but misses it.
A full ball, on middle. Paul Stirling looks to push it down the ground but gets inner half towards mid-wicket.
A length ball, way outside off. Left alone.
BEATEN! A good length ball, angling around off. Andy Balbirnie looks to defend inside the line but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Just a single! A good length ball, outside off. Paul Stirling opens his bat face and steers it down to third man for one.
Outside off, on a length. Paul Stirling shoulders arms to it.
Another full ball, on off. Paul Stirling drives it straight to mid off.
Touch fuller, around off. This is pushed to covers for a single.
BEATEN! Nortje bowls a length ball, just around off, straightens up off the deck. Paul Stirling plays inside the line and misses it.
LEG BYE! A back of a length ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie hops and looks to clip it but misses. Gets hit on the pads and the boll rolls over to the leg side.
A pacy short ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie ducks under it.
A good length ball, around middle. Defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Good shot! Andy Balbirnie picking it up from where he left off in the last game! Nortje pitches it up, on off. Andy Balbirnie lunges forward and creams it through covers for a boundary.
A good length ball, on middle. Andy Balbirnie drives it off the outer half of his balde towards point.
Who will use the other new ball? Anrich Nortje it is! Two slips in place.
FOUR! First boundary of the innings! A short ball, outside off. Paul Stirling hops and slashes it over the point fielder for a boundary.
Touch fuller, on middle and leg. Paul Stirling looks to flick but misses, gets hit on the pads and the ball rolls over to the off side. Looks like he got an inside edge on that one.
A length ball, angling on middle. Andy Balbirnie looks to defend from his crease but gets an inside edge towards leg side for a single. He is off the mark as well.
Good length ball, wide outside off, shapes away as well. Andy Balbirnie leaves it to the keeper.
Ireland and Paul Stirling are off the mark! A length ball, on middle. Stirling flicks it on the leg side of a single.
Kagiso Rabada starts with a wayward delivery, outside off. Paul Stirling leaves it alone to the keeper.
It is cloudy out there, but the sun is peeking through at times. It is expected to stay the same throughout the course of the game.

We are set for the action to begin! The South African fielders jog out to the middle. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie walk out to bat. The players take the knee to protest against racial discrimination. Kagiso Rabada to start with the ball!

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish skipper, says that the first game went pretty well but it wasn't easy with the overhead conditions. Informs that Potterfield misses out due to an infection on his finger and Curtis Campher comes in. Informs that he will bat at the top of the order.

Temba Bavuma, the South Africa skipper, says that the first game gave them a chance to understand the conditions. Adds that it might be difficult to defend so they will bowl first. Informs that Anrich Nortje is in for Lungi Ngidi.
PITCH REPORT - Nial O'Brien says that the pitch is dry. Says the pacers will benefit at the start and later it will be better to bat on.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Curtis Campher (In for William Porterfield), Andy Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, George Dockrell, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Andy McBrine, Simi Singh, Josh Little, Craig Young, Mark Adair.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Janneman Malan, Temba Bavuma (C), Rassie van der Dussen, Kyle Verreynne (WK), David Miller, Andile Phehlukwayo, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje (In for Lungi Ngidi), Tabraiz Shamsi.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of South Africa. They have ELECTED TO BOWL FIRST!

Hello and a warm welcome to the second ODI between Ireland and South Africa. It is essentially a two-match series as the first game was washed out due to rain. The teams will have to win both games if they want to win the series. Will we see changes being made in the sides? Who will win the toss and will rain play a part in the game? We will find out and once again a very warm welcome!
